0.long_answer: Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis is an autoimmune disorder in which antibodies target NMDA receptors in the brain. In approximately half of affected women, the condition is associated with an ovarian teratoma—a type of germ cell tumor that can contain several types of tissue, including hair, teeth, or bone. The presence of neural tissue within these teratomas may trigger the immune system to produce antibodies against NMDA receptors, leading to encephalitis. Surgical removal of the teratoma often improves the clinical outcome by eliminating the source of the immune trigger.
